Syed Mahmud Hossain, Advocate  ----- For the Petitioner: 
Nikhilesh Dutra, Advocate  ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Makbul Ahmed and others  ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Mohammedullah and others  ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of judgment and order dated, 15-7-86 passed by the Additional District Judge Noakhali in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 153/84 refusing to interfere with the order dated 16-9-84 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 324/80 recording the order of the High Court Division dated 7-12-83. 

 2. The opposite parties as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 545176 in the Court of Subordinate Judge for declaration of title, which was decreed ex parte on 29-9-80 and the present petitioner on 11-11-80 filed an application under Order IX rule 13. CPC being Miscellaneous Case No. 324 of 1980 for setting aside the ex parte decree. The plaintiffs opposite parties contested the case by filing joint written objection and the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali by his judgment and order dated 9-12-82 dismissed the Miscellaneous Case consequently the petition under Order IX rule 13, CPC was rejected. The present petitioner thereafter preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13/83 before the High Court Division and the High Court Division by judgment dated 7-12-83 allowed the appeal setting aside the order dated 9-12-82 passed by the Subordinate Judge and thereby allowed the application under Order IX rule 13, CPC and the suit was restored to its original file and number. It was ordered by the High Court Division that the defendants shall pay to the plaintiffs as cost Taka 1,000 within 2 months from the date of arrival of the record in the trial Court failing which the appeal shall stand dismissed. 

 3. The trial Court received the case record on 14-7-84 and fixed the case on 12-9-84 and directed the defendants’ petitioner to deposit Taka 1,000 and further ordered to inform the petitioners. It appears from the order dated 14-7-84 that the appointed Advocates of the parties endorsed the order having noted the word seen on 21-7-34. The learned subordinate judge passed the order in the following terms: 

 No deposit as per direction of the Hon'ble High Court Comilla Bench vide order passed in FMA 13/83 has yet been made though duly informed and the stipulated period for depositing the cost by defendant appellant has already lapsed. Hence the First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13/83 of the High Court Division Comilla Bench stands dismissed. 

 5. It appears from the record that the defendant petitioners filed an application under section 151 of the Code Of Civil Procedure on 26-9-84 supported by affidavit praying for vesting the order dated 16-9-84 stating that the petitioners were not informed about the arrival of the record of the case from the High Court Division and by filing another applications the petitioner prayed that he may be allowed to deposit the money by challan according to the order made by the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal but the petition was rejected on the said date. The petitioners thereafter being wrongly advised proffered the Miscellaneous Appeal on 30-9-84 before the District Judge Noakhali being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 153/84 which was disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge by the impugned judgment and order finding that the appeal is not maintainable for inasmuch as the learned Subordinate Judge merely recorded the order of dismissal after the expiry of two months as prescribed in the judgment of the High Court Division. It has been stated that the petitioners enquired from the bench clerk about the arrival of the case record from the High Court Division having failed to get any information filed an application for information on 3-9-84 and on that the petitioner was informed on 20-9-84 that the FMA No. 13/83 stood dismissed on 16-9-84. It has been contended that the trial Court should have corrected its own mistake under section 151 of the CPC as it is evident from the order dated 14-7-84 that the proper information to the petitioners as to the arrival of the case record was not made in accordance with the provision of law and it was incumbent upon the trial Court to communicate to the petitioner as to the arrival of the record from the High Court. It has been further contended that the court order dated 14-7-84 which was endorsed by the appointed Advocate is not the proper information in accordance with law as his power or vokalatnama was terminated after the disposal of the Miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13, CPC. It is further argued that Mr A Sobhan was not in charge of the case under Order IX rule 13, CPC. The learned Advocate has emphatically submitted that it was incumbent on the court to inform the parties concerned about the arrival of the record by issuing notice to the parties. Mr Syed Mahmud Hossain has referred to Order III rule 4(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure and pointed out that as the proceedings under Order IX rule 13 CPC were ended after the disposal of the case the learned Advocate who got the order signed on 14-7-84 ceased to be the appointed Advocate of the petitioners and any information given to the said appointed Advocate is no information is the eye of law. 

 (2) Every such appointment shall be filed in court and shall be deemed to be in force until determined with the leave of the court by a writing signed by the client or the pleader, as the case may be, and filed in court, or until the client or the pleader dies, or until all proceedings in the suit are ended so far as regards the client. 

 7. Mr Mahmud Hossain has also referred to a decision in the case of MA Wahab and another vs Abul Kalam and another reported in 44 DLR (AD) 13 where rule 388(2) of the CRO and several decisions of this court in interpretation of the said rules were discussed. In the case of Mohammed Ramzan Sawadagor vs AHM Fazlul Huq. 15 DLR 99 the observation was made in the following terms which has been quoted in the decision of the A ppellate Division as referred to above: 

 "This rule contemplates that if on the date fixed any important order is passed this order is to be signed by a pleader and endeavour should be made to get the signature of the pleader. But if an order is passed on an off date in a case not appearing in the cause list or on a date not fixed for a case. it is still more incumbent on the court to see that the order is communicated". 

 7. Admittedly, as it appears from the order dated 14-7-84, the record of the case was received by the learned subordinate judge on the said date and the next date was fixed 12-9-84 for depositing the cost and it was ordered to inform, and the court got the order signed by the learned advocates of the respective parties. It is asserted by the petitioners placing the materials that Mr Abdus Sobhan was no longer the appointed Advocate for the petitioners and that in such circumstances it was incumbent upon the court to communicate the order to the parties the petitioners about the arrival of the record of the case. It is further seen that the petitioners filed an application for information on 3-9-84 which was not replied in due time and the petitioner was informed on 20-9-84 to the effect that the dismissal order has been recorded on 16-9-84. In that view it cannot be reasonably said that the petitioner failed to deposit the money or that he did not take any step as has been found by the learned subordinate Judge in his order dated 12-9-84. 

 9. The learned Additional District Judge appeared to have passed the impugned order which is in accord with the principle of law because no appeal lies against the order dated 16-9-84. But the error that has been committed causing failure of justice must be corrected by this court by exercising power under section 115 of the Code and also by exercising inherent power as contemplated under section 151 of the Code. The trial Court should have corrected the mistake on the application filed by the petitioner on 26-9-84 under section 151 of the CP Code which was rejected but no revision case was brought against that order. Since the order dated 16- 9-84 is not appealable the order passed by learned Additional District Judge need not be set aside. 

 10. Now the question that arises before me is, as to whether the High Court is in a position to rectify such error or mistake in the instant proceeding. The principle is well settled now. Under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure this court is invested with the power to make such order in a case as it thinks fit. Furthermore section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure codefies the well-established legal principle that every court has inherent power to act ex debito justitiae so that real and substantial justice for which alone the court exists, or to prevent abuse of the process of the court. The courts are to act upon the principle and every procedure furthering the cause of justice is to be understood as permissible till it is shown to be prohibited by the law. The inherent powers referred to in section 151 of the Code are such as are used to secure the ends of justice or to prevent the abuse of the process of the court (see 34 DLR 325). 

 11. Mr Nikhilesh Dutta, the learned Counsel appearing for the opposite parties, pointed out the orders dated 14-7-84, 12-9-84 and 16-9-84 and has submitted that since the orders were signed by the appointed Advocate for the petitioners it was within the knowledge of the petitioners about the arrival of the record in the trial Court and that the petitioner having failed to deposit the cost within stipulated time the trial Court was justified in recording the order of dismissal according to the judgment of the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal. 

 13. For the foregoing reasons the Rule is made absolute. The orders dated 12-9-94 and 16-9-84 are set aside. The learned Subordinate Judge is directed to communicate the order to the concerned parties after arrival of the record in that court and fix a date for depositing the cost within the time as mentioned in the judgment dated 7-12-83 passed in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 13 of 1983. 

 14. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case there will be no order as to costs.
